Current blobs: (18,29) [blob1 has moved], (18,35) [blob3], (24,41) [blob4], (36,41) [blob5].
Wait — where's blob2? Originally it was at (18,23). It's gone! The diff from frame 12 showed N→w at (18,24-25), (19,23-26), (20,23-26), (21,24-25) — blob2 disappeared when I clicked blob1's target!
So: when blob1 jumped from (18,17) to (18,29), it passed over blob2 at (18,23) → blob2 got erased (collision!). And blob1 landed at (18,29) and survived.
Now it all fits! The frame 6 event: blob2 jumped from (18,23) to (18,11), passing over blob1 at (18,17) → blob1 erased, and blob2 itself also… erased? Hmm, blob2 also disappeared in frame 6. And gray dots appeared at (18,11), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41).
Hmm, wait, in frame 6 blob2 also disappeared. But this time blob1 (the jumper) survived. The difference: in frame 6 the jump was leftward (18,23)→(18,11); this time it was rightward (18,17)→(18,29).
And in frame 6, gray dots appeared at the positions of blobs 3/4/5 (which didn't move) and at (18,11) (the landing point). This time no gray dots appeared at all.
Hmm, what else was different in frame 6? In frame 6, before the click, both blob1 and blob2 had been selected (blob1 in frame 2, then blob2 in frame 4). Maybe the game tracks "selection history": when you click a target, the selected blob jumps, and all previously selected blobs get erased?? In frame 6: previously selected = {blob1, blob2}; the jumper = blob2; result: blob1 erased (previously selected), blob2… also erased? Hmm, no, blob2 is the jumper.
Wait, maybe: the jumper also gets erased if it passes over a previously selected blob? In frame 6, blob2 passed over blob1 (previously selected) → both erased. This time, blob1 passed over blob2 (never selected) → only blob2 erased? But why would passing over a non-selected blob erase it?
Hmm, or maybe the rule is simply "the jump erases all blobs on the path" (this time: blob2 erased; frame 6: blob1 erased), and additionally in frame 6 the jumper also got erased because… the landing cell (18,11) was… hmm, (18,11) was empty.
Wait, wait. Let me re-verify the frame 6 landing: was the gray dot at (18,11) the landing point of the erased jumper? And the gray dots at (18,35), (24,41), (36,41) = "scars" at the positions of the other blobs?? Why would the other blobs leave scars?
Hmm, maybe the gray dots in frame 6 are something else entirely. Let me look at the frame 6 image… I don't have it on hand, but the current image after the key click (frame 9) was the restored initial state. The frame 6 image showed 4 gray dots (hollow rings) and a key.
New idea: maybe the gray dots in frame 6 are "ghosts" of erased blobs: blob1 erased at (18,17)?? No, the dots were at (18,11), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41).
Ugh. Okay, let me think about what (18,35), (24,41), (36,41) have in common: they're the positions of blobs 3, 4, 5. And (18,11) is blob2's landing point. So in frame 6: blob2 landed at (18,11) (gray dot = "settled" blob?), blobs 3/4/5 became gray dots (settled?), and blobs 1/2… wait, blob2 is the jumper that landed at (18,11) — so the dot at (18,11) is blob2 in "settled" state! And blobs 3/4/5 also settled (turned gray). And blob1 got erased (passed over).
So the rule might be: "when a blob jumps, all blobs settle (turn gray), except… no, this time (frame 12) blobs 3/4/5 stayed green.
The difference between frame 6 and frame 12: in frame 6, the jumper (blob2) passed over blob1, and blob1 had been previously selected. In frame 12, the jumper (blob1) passed over blob2, which had never been selected.
Maybe: "passing over a previously selected blob" causes a catastrophe (everything settles + key appears as undo). "Passing over a non-selected blob" just erases that blob.
Hmm, that's oddly specific. Or:
Frame 6: the jump path (18,23)→(18,11) passes over (18,17) [blob1] and (18,11) is… the path cells: 18,22; 18,21; 18,20; 18,19; 18,18; 18,17 [blob1]; 18,16; 18,15; 18,14; 18,13; 18,12. Only blob1 is on the path.
Frame 12: the path (18,17)→(18,29) passes over (18,18)…(18,28): blob2 at (18,23) is on the path. Only blob2.
So both jumps passed over exactly one blob. Frame 6: the jumped-over blob (blob1) + the jumper (blob2) both erased, the other 3 settled gray, key appeared. Frame 12: the jumped-over blob (blob2) erased, the jumper (blob1) survived, the others unchanged.
The only difference I can identify: in frame 6, blob1 (the jumped-over one) had been previously selected.
Or the difference is: the direction of the jump? Left vs right? That seems arbitrary.
Or: in frame 6, I had previously clicked (19,12) in frame 1 (before selecting anything) — a no-op. Hmm.
Or: in frame 6, the order of selection was: select blob1, then select blob2 (switching selection). In frame 12, blob1 was freshly selected (after the key restoration, I clicked blob1 in frame 10). Maybe "switching selection" is what matters: when you switch from blob A to blob B, blob A gets marked as "erased on next jump"?
Whatever the exact rule, the practical lesson is: don't jump over other blobs. The goal is probably to place all 5 blobs on their respective targets. But wait — when blob1 jumped to (18,29), did it "complete"? It's still green. Maybe green = active, and the goal is to turn all blobs gray (settled)? In frame 6, 3 blobs settled gray but 2 were erased — that was a failed attempt (hence the key/undo).
Hmm, but how do blobs settle without catastrophe? Maybe a blob settles (turns gray) when it jumps to its target without passing over any other blob? In frame 12, blob1 jumped to (18,29) but passed over blob2, so it stayed green (failed).
So the correct strategy: order the jumps so that no jump passes over another blob. The blobs are at (18,29) [blob1], (18,35) [blob3], (24,41) [blob4], (36,41) [blob5]. Blob2 is gone (erased) — damn, I've lost one blob. Can I restore it? The key is gone. Hmm.
Wait, is blob2 really gone, or did it move? The current blobs: (18,29), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41). The original 5: (18,17), (18,23), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41). Blob1 (18,17) → now at (18,29). Blob2 (18,23) → erased. So 4 blobs remain.
Hmm, wait, but maybe the level doesn't require all 5. Maybe the goal is just "place the blobs on their targets" and the erased blob2 is a problem. Or maybe the goal is something else entirely, like "clear all blobs" (turn them all gray)?
Let me think about the targets: blob1's target (18,29) — blob1 is there now. Blob2's target (18,11). What are the targets of blobs 3/4/5? I need to select each one and check.
Let me select blob3 (18,35) and look at its target ring. Then blob4 (24,41), blob5 (36,41).
Note: selecting a blob is safe (just shows the ring). The risk is clicking the target while another blob is on the path.
Current positions: blob1 (18,29), blob3 (18,35), blob4 (24,41), blob5 (36,41).
If blob3's target is, say, (18,41) or (18,47): the path (18,35)→(18,47) passes over (18,41) — empty. No problem.
Let me check the targets of blobs 3, 4, 5.
